name: Process Monitor
description: A task manager scoped to TEDI, in the short version: TEDI itself and the terminals you opened. Nothing is hidden, only summed - the WebView2 children, the extension sidecars and everything a shell went on to start are added to the row that owns them, so a terminal weighs what it and its whole subtree weigh and the column still adds up to the entire tree. AI CLIs attached to a terminal (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, opencode and friends) badge and name the terminal they run in. Memory is the private working set, the same number Task Manager shows, so the two agree instead of differing by the shared Chromium pages seven WebView2 processes hold in common. Because a total that size is mostly what you started rather than what TEDI costs, the app's own share - the window, its WebView2 processes and the PTY daemon - is shown beside the total in the pane header and on the status-bar hover, and a row's tooltip says what the process it names weighs on its own: a shell reading 1.9G is a 36M shell holding an agent. The status bar carries the tree total and a live CPU reading; clicking it opens the rows. Reads the OS process table once per poll; nothing is killed, written or sent anywhere.
author: IlhamRiski - ilhamriski.com
